data.description:
## Context / Problem
After S2, help and identity come from the route registry while real execution still traverses the explicit intercept/dispatch ladders and policy frozensets. Leaving those authorities in parallel would preserve the coordination defect RP-05 is intended to remove.

## Approach
Move core top-level execution to the selected registry route after the pre-operation help boundary. Resolve only the selected lazy `module:function` reference and invoke it through a closed, typed adapter-kind set matching existing call shapes. Keep all command-specific argument parsing inside current handlers.

Consume route metadata for:

- central best-effort mount eligibility;
- strict initialization `none`, `init_only`, or `full`, plus the two existing narrow selectors for conditional cases;
- position-independent confirmation/output extraction while preserving tokens after `--`;
- legacy output passthrough for `create`, `idea`, `transition`, `claim`, and `reopen`;
- exact argv, stdout/stderr, exit-code, and exception contracts.

Before cutover, compare registry-derived policies to every existing policy set and dispatch arm. Any non-allowlisted delta fails shadow parity. Cut over one selected route authority only after parity is exact; keep S2's derived compatibility exports for rollback until S6.

This story covers core and bridge execution that does not change optional-capability posture. S4 owns selected optional mode/backend checks and can proceed from the same S2 contract without editing this story's domain seams.

## Compatibility and Rollback
The positive rationale is a single validated selection/dispatch authority while preserving specialized handlers. No generic signature introspection or middleware pipeline is added. Rollback switches execution lookup to the derived compatibility exports; no event, ticket, bridge, or binding data changes.

## Testing
Use real CLI subprocess contract tests rather than source greps for routing behavior. Extend existing mount/init, mutation confirmation, global output, bridge vocabulary, hidden alias, unknown, and exit-code suites. Add typed fake handlers for every invocation-adapter kind and selectors. Include negative controls for tokens after `--`, malformed global flags, no-auto-mount commands, store-touching intercepts, and handler exceptions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every core canonical command and compatibility spelling resolves exactly one lazy handler through a closed adapter kind, and only the selected handler module is imported.
- [ ] Registry-derived mount/init behavior matches the pre-cutover shadow census for every route, including no-auto-mount and conditional-selector cases.
- [ ] Confirmation, global output extraction, legacy JSON shapes, argv after `--`, streams, exit codes, and exception propagation match the existing behavioral tests.
- [ ] Bridge compatibility spellings and hidden `bridge-status` execute through their approved canonical adapters while `purge-bridge` remains unknown.
- [ ] Execution can be switched back to the derived compatibility exports without changing persisted data or handler interfaces.
data.title: RP-05 S3 — Dispatch core CLI execution through validated lazy routes
